neighbours.label: In quoted conversation, the token just before a hedged opinion or knowledge verb is expected: "I don't" (→ think / know), "I" before suppose, "do you" (→ think)
fire: She shook her head slowly. "No, I don't think he meant any harm by it."
"Is the bridge still open?" asked the driver. "I don't know, to be honest," said the boy.
"Could we finish by Friday?" "Well, I suppose we could, if nothing breaks."
He frowned at the map. "Honestly, I don't think this is the right road."
"What do you think she wanted?" asked Tom, leaning on the fence.
"Was that your cousin at the door?" "Oh, I don't know who it was."
The old man scratched his ear. "Aye, I suppose you're right about that."
"Shall we tell her tonight?" "Hmm, I don't think that's wise."
quiet: She shook her head slowly and walked back to the barn with the bucket.
"Is the bridge still open?" asked the driver. "Yes, until nine tonight," said the boy.
"Hand me the hammer," he said. "Here, take the nails too."
He frowned at the map and folded it back into his coat pocket.
"Close the gate behind you," called Tom, leaning on the fence.
"Was that your cousin at the door?" "Yes, she brought the eggs."
The old man scratched his ear and poured another cup of tea.
"Dinner is at seven," she said. "Bring the bread and the wine."

notes: Card: '’t' x10, ' I', ' you', dialogue openers; reversed output promotes ' you', ' probably', ' suppose', ' realize'. Probes: "I don't think" 0.43, "I suppose" 0.40, "do you think" 0.22, "I don't know" 0.21; "I don't eat meat" 0.10, narration 0.01.
